parallel.requirements: Recognized the Python idna CLI, ESM .mjs output, manual process.argv parsing, zero external dependencies, no Python embedding, and no url/punycode interface constraints.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent spawned a probe child, the child spawned a nested probe, and both parent and child worked in the shared /output area; parent retained final ownership after rejecting the child deliverable.
parallel.implementation: Child first built a modular wrapper around the reference executable; parent later deleted that bridge and implemented local parser, Punycode, Unicode, IDNA, output, and main modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact list contains test8.mjs plus local library modules; integration included replacement of child-written /output/test8.mjs and deletion of reference_runner.mjs.
parallel.verification: Parent ran spot checks, broad differential sweeps, randomized domain comparisons, and parser edge checks after the self-contained replacement, reporting stdout/stderr/exit-code parity on tested cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation remained failed at 19/20. The visible parallel-specific defect was earlier child wrapper output that had to be overwritten, not the final hidden failing test itself.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argv parsing, pure JavaScript, local-import-only, no Python and no prohibited built-in interface requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent performed source inspection, executable probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without child ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: Built local ESM modules for CLI parsing, errors, formatting, Punycode, Unicode/IDNA validation, warnings, and the test8.mjs entrypoint without delegating to the executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a single coherent final tree of eight files under /output with the required entrypoint and local library imports.
serial.verification: Ran sample checks, parser failures, abbreviation and attached-option cases, malformed A-labels, contextual code points, and length-boundary parity sweeps against the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed at 19/20 despite broad parity checks; no serial coordination failure is present because this is the single-agent control.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, local-import-only, no Python, and no url/punycode interface requirements, and ultimately claimed a self-contained port.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt constraints and delivered a self-contained ESM module hierarchy with manual argv behavior and no external packages.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement coverage at final was similar, but the parallel child initially violated the self-contained/no-reference-executable spirit before the parent corrected it; serial did not take that detour.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by spawning a probe child and nested probe, while the parent continued probing and later owned the final rewrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child activity and kept probing, implementation, verification, and delivery in one agent path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created overlapping deliverable ownership in /output; serial avoided cross-agent ownership boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child had task context and returned a result admitting the bridge/wrapper nature; the parent received that information and acted on it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained requirements and interface assumptions locally, using measured executable behavior directly in its own implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The issue was not lost context or an omitted contract; it was a child deliverable that failed the known implementation boundary and had to be rejected.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first received a wrapper implementation, then the parent replaced it with local IDNA, Unicode, Punycode, parser, and output modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial directly implemented local ESM modules for the same behavior without a wrapper phase.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost time to an invalid implementation path before converging on a self-contained implementation; serial followed the self-contained path from the implementation patch onward.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed and returned its result; the parent received the handoff, inspected the files, and explicitly rejected the wrapper output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; implementation and final response remained in the same session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's lifecycle includes a completed child result that is joined only to be discarded; serial has no comparable join/rejection step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child wrote the submitted entrypoint and libraries into shared /output, then the parent observed those files and replaced/deleted parts of that tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one final tree itself and did not have concurrent agents writing or replacing the submitted entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state deliverable overwrite episode; serial had a linear write path with no cross-agent artifact collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After replacing the wrapper, parallel ran spot checks, a broad comparison that reached zero mismatches, and randomized differential tests that ended with zero mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran repeated parity sweeps covering samples, parser errors, length, Unicode, A-label, and bool parsing cases, then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified substantially and both missed one official hidden case; verification breadth does not explain an official outcome difference because there is none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed more time and tool activity, with three subagent rollouts and a rework step, but still completed without timeout and delivered artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with no subagents, no child wait/rework, and one final artifact tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel overhead was adverse process cost rather than an outcome differentiator; both completed official evaluation at 19/20.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show no discordant outcome: both parallel and serial failed, each passing 19 of 20 official samples. The concrete process difference is that the parallel child produced a prohibited wrapper deliverable and the parent overwrote it, while the serial run implemented a self-contained ESM stack directly. That overwrite caused rework and invalidated child implementation output, but the final official scores are the same, so it is not an evidenced cause of an outcome split.
parallel_contributors: Child wrote a wrapper-based submitted entrypoint that the parent later discarded and replaced with a self-contained implementation.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation ownership local and avoided cross-agent writes to /output/test8.mjs.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final solutions used different local module organizations and both missed one hidden official testcase despite broad parity checks.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event, not a cause of a discordant official result

candidates.reason: Implementation was owned: the parent probed and later implemented the ESM IDNA stack, while the child also attempted a deliverable; the issue was over-writing, not no implementer.
The parent explicitly inspected the child output and reconciled it by replacing it, so integration responsibility was present rather than absent.
Both child and parent placed an entrypoint in /output, and the final artifact was assembled; the adverse event was a submitted-entrypoint overwrite.
The parent owned the end-to-end path through probing, implementation, verification, and final response; no unowned pipeline transition is evidenced.
Productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory preflight; the child was active while the parent probed, and the realized issue was a conflicting deliverable write.
The parallel run did not merely finish all investigation before implementation; a child wrote implementation files during the run, and the later consequence was overwrite/rework.
The parent completed the self-contained implementation and verification after taking over; there is no direct evidence that essential implementation capacity was starved.
Only two spawn calls and three child threads are recorded, the run did not time out, and the final failure is not traced to collective fan-out budget exhaustion.
The child completed and returned a wrapper-based deliverable; its defect was an invalid implementation choice, not unfinished work caused by an overbroad assignment.
The child trajectory contains the same task prompt context and the child acknowledged a full hand-coded IDNA port as a separate option; omission from the brief is not proven.
The agents were not producing separately owned components meant to interoperate under an omitted interface contract; they produced competing whole deliverables.
The child final reached the parent and identified the wrapper/bridge nature; the parent acted on that information rather than losing it.
The child report was available and actionable; the parent inspected the files and replaced them, so volume did not prevent consumption.
The child result described the current wrapper files that still existed when the parent inspected them; it was unacceptable, not stale.
No unadjudicated incompatible reports remained at a decision point; the parent resolved the conflict by rejecting and replacing the wrapper output.
The parent ran integrated parity checks after replacing the wrapper and no parent-visible unresolved integrated gap remained before final; hidden evaluator failure alone is insufficient.
There was no replacement retry child that repeated work without inherited findings; the parent takeover used its own probes and inspected child artifacts.

candidates.reason: No child was explicitly stopped before finishing; both child trajectories reached task_complete/final states.
No complete valid candidate was left unpromoted; the child candidate was a prohibited wrapper and the parent placed a final self-contained tree.
The parent performed verification after replacing the wrapper output, including broad differential and randomized checks.
The delegated implementation was retrieved and inspected by the parent, then explicitly rejected; this is not an unjoined result.
No verifier child produced a finding that was trapped below the parent; the nested probe returned through the child and the child result reached the parent.
The child did not abort or get cancelled, and the parent did take over the invalid wrapper by replacing it with a self-contained implementation.
The parent did not ignore the completed child result; it inspected the child-written files and explicitly rejected the wrapper approach.
Although one wait call used an invalid short timeout, the parent continued active probing and later inspected child progress before finalizing; no blind wait to deadline occurred.
The agents produced overlapping implementations, but a same deliverable replacement is directly proven and is more specific.
The same submitted entrypoint was replaced, but the taxonomy gives Deliverable Overwrite precedence for an entrypoint/source deliverable.
Non-entry library sources were deleted or rewritten, but the episode also replaced the required entrypoint, so Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific retained label.

A child wrote /output/test8.mjs and wrapper library files as the deliverable, then the parent inspected and replaced that submitted entrypoint and module tree because it violated the self-contained requirement.

The parent inspected child artifacts to reject them, not to consume them as stable reference input for implementation or verification.
